title: Oil Surges as US Strikes Iran After Hormuz Tanker Attacks
content: On 7-8 July 2026, US forces struck more than 80 Iranian targets after tankers were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, a route handling roughly a fifth of global oil and gas trade. Brent crude jumped 5.2% to settle at $78.02/bbl on 8 July, while WTI rose 4.4% to $73.52, reversing a slide back toward pre-conflict levels. Iran called the strikes a breach of last month's ceasefire understanding with Washington. UK gilt yields and broader rates markets also moved as traders raised bets on the policy response to a renewed energy shock, keeping a geopolitical risk premium embedded across commodities, equities and FX.

title: Fed Minutes Reveal Hawkish Tilt as Rate-Hike Camp Grows to Nine
content: Minutes from the Fed's 16-17 June meeting, released 8 July 2026, showed nine of 18 policymakers now favour a rate hike this year, up from a March dot plot that had pointed to cuts. New chair Kevin Warsh, in his first meeting, issued a stripped-down policy statement without forward guidance or his own dot, keeping tactics deliberately vague. Officials were split, with some seeing scope for easing if inflation cools and others warning further tightening may be needed. UST yields rose and the USD firmed on the "higher-for-longer" signal, pressuring gold and adding volatility to equities, as futures markets pushed year-end Fed funds expectations toward 4%.

title: China CPI Cools to 3-Month Low as PPI Hits 4-Year High
content: China's June CPI rose just 1% y/y, data released 9 July 2026 showed, below the 1.1% forecast and down from May's 1.2%, as fuel-price cuts weighed on non-food inflation. PPI accelerated to 4.1% y/y, its strongest since July 2022, though it fell 0.3% m/m, widening the gap between factory-gate and consumer prices and squeezing downstream margins. The PBoC left benchmark LPRs unchanged for a 13th straight month, reaffirming "appropriately loose" policy while flagging "structural divergence" between AI-driven growth and weak consumption. The data reinforced deflation concerns weighing on the yuan and raised questions over China's recovery, with implications for global growth and commodity demand.
